And having stood [as king] for four months, he died.
And in that same year, which was the year 997

And his son Justinian reigned for ten years.
[Ibn] Zubayr, eight years and four months.
This man was in Yathrib [Medina], as we have said;
and in his days there was a great schism among the Arabs.
In Babel, indeed, a man named 'Abdallah rebelled;
and in Resh'aina, a man named Hukkab (or Hubab);
and a certain Burayda in Nisibis;
and 'Umar ibn Sa'id in Damascus;
and a certain Zufar in Circesium.
The Mardaites of the Romans who were in Lebanon were also raiding everywhere.
And while this schism remained among them for about eight years,
the people of Damascus proclaimed as king over them 'Abd al-Malik, the son of Marwan, the son of Hakam.
Twenty-first.
[Abd al-Malik son of] Marwan, thirteen years and six months.
And he was called 'the Father of Flies',
because the gaps between his teeth smelled foul,
and when he kept his mouth open,
flies would gather on his mouth.
When this man was proclaimed king,
and he saw that wars surrounded him on all sides,
and was especially hard-pressed by the Mardaites of the Romans who were in Lebanon,
he made peace with Justinian for ten years:
that Justinian should withdraw his raiders, who numbered twelve thousand, from the land of the Arabs,
and in return for this 'Abd al-Malik should give to the Romans each day a thousand dinars, and one horse, and one slave;
and that Cyprus should remain neutral (in the middle),
half of the tribute going to the Romans and half to the Arabs;
and that Armenia, together with Georgia, Arzan, and Azerbaijan, should belong to the Romans.
And when peace was established,
'Abd al-Malik waged war against Ibn Zubayr and defeated him.
And when Ibn Zubayr fled and entered Yathrib [Medina] and fortified himself in the house in which they pray,
a certain commander called Hajjaj pursued him,
and set up mangonels against the house and tore down the wall,
and entered and killed Ibn Zubayr,
and rebuilt the house.
